Astor.opium_activity: Smuggled hundreds of thousands of pounds of opium into China (1810s)
Astor.exit: 1825 - invested profits in New York real estate

Cabot.opium_activity: China opium market participation; "exploitative business ventures" (Britannica)
Cabot.connections: Boston Brahmins; Senator Henry Cabot Lodge (nephew)

Peabody.opium_activity: East India trade; "extremely wealthy" from Asian trade; museum notes "profits derived from illegal trade in opium"
Peabody.connections: George Peabody became London financier; sponsored North American railroads

Perkins-Cushing.opium_activity: By 1815 set up European offices to buy Turkish opium for Canton; "turned to smuggling Turkish opium into China"; worked with Chinese hong merchants (Howqua)
Perkins-Cushing.connections: John P. Cushing = T.H. Perkins nephew; John Murray Forbes became junior partner; Cushing married into Low family

Coolidge-Heard.opium_activity: Partner in Heard & Co.; decades trading opium, silk, tea; headed Canton operations (1840s)
Coolidge-Heard.connections: Joseph married Thomas Jefferson's granddaughter; T.J. Coolidge married into Lowell mills; Warren Delano descendants include President Calvin Coolidge

Weld.opium_activity: Ran clipper fleets carrying opium; later patriarch: "all our ancestors were opium smugglers—pretty much the family business"
legacy: Harvard Boathouse (G.W. Weld = "greatest benefactor Harvard ever had in rowing")
Weld.connections: Intermarried with Perkins, Cabot; David Weld (Gov. Weld descendant) confirms family lore

firms: Russell & Co. (Canton) - head of Canton office, majority stake
Delano.opium_activity: Joined Russell & Co. 1833; became head of Canton office; "outdistanced every other American company in opium holdings"; profited from First Opium War; returned during Civil War to ship opium to U.S. Army medical service
legacy: Town of Delano, PA (co-founder with Asa Packer)
Federal Reserve (nephew F.A. Delano = first vice-chairman)
Delano.connections: Daughter married into Forbes family; granddaughter Sara married James Roosevelt (FDR mother); related to Astors and Coolidges; nephew F.A. Delano married Packer family
Delano.significance: FDR's maternal grandfather - direct presidential link to opium trade

Brown.opium_activity: Ran ships to Canton; "active in China trade" and slave trade
legacy: Providence Bank (1791) - forerunner of Citizens Bank
Brown University (College of Rhode Island renamed)
Brown.connections: Brothers Moses and Nicholas; intermarried with Rhode Island elites (Standish family)

Heard.opium_activity: Third-largest US China firm; introduced steamships to China
legacy: Nephews became ministers and bankers; wealth dissipated after 1870s crash
Heard.connections: Founded with partner Joseph Coolidge; nephews intermarried with Forbes and Lull families

Russell & Company.description: Largest American opium-trading house in Canton
key_people: Warren Delano Jr. (head of Canton office, majority stake)
Russell & Company.significance: Dominant American firm in opium trade; "outdistanced every other American company in opium holdings"

Perkins & Co..operations: European offices to buy Turkish opium for Canton; worked with Chinese hong merchant Howqua

Universities & Education: Brown University (renamed from College of Rhode Island; John Brown major donor)
Harvard University (Cabot, Weld, Coolidge endowments; buildings, boathouse, art)
Perkins School for Blind (Thomas H. Perkins)
Hospitals & Medical: Massachusetts General Hospital (Thomas H. Perkins land donor)
Museums & Cultural: Astor Library (precursor to New York Public Library)
Boston Museum of Fine Arts (Perkins-Cushing, Weld collections)
Peabody Essex Museum (Asian art from opium profits)
Infrastructure & Finance: Providence Bank (1791, John Brown) - forerunner of Citizens Bank
Granite Railway (Perkins investment) - for Bunker Hill Monument
Town of Delano, PA (Warren Delano Jr. + Asa Packer)
Federal Reserve (Frederic Adrian Delano = first vice-chairman)
